why: Shoulder abducted to 90 degrees (arm horizontal), front view. Outer: the arm's top line runs into the deltoid cap as one convex curve without a ledge (no step or shelf where the arm meets the shoulder), the cap rising a little over the joint (the deltoid contracted, o 1.04 of the arm's own rest half-width at the joint), then into the trapezius slope toward the neck, which the arm does not move: that part is her own rest outline (rays from the joint 25-75 degrees from up, medially). Inner: the arm's underside line, unchanged from rest. NOT scored: the armpit and the front axillary fold, and the trunk's side below it (the rest A-pose hides them, so the body gives no scale; the lead authors them on the new base).
grammar: Control points in the strip's side view (tools/body/bends.py build_ref): seg p|d, s = fraction of that segment's rest length from the joint, side in|out, o = multiple of the body's OWN rest half-width there (measured on its rest strip), mm = added millimetres; line = the half-width extrapolated straight from two stations; arc = the outer corner swept from the proximal to the distal outer normal (fraction), corner = the two offset lines' meeting point (mm_bisect pushes it into the open sector: a web), tip = a bony point carried with the distal bone, sharp = a corner the smoothing keeps. Away from the joint o=1: the limb keeps its rest shape (a rigid bend); only the joint's own anatomy is authored.
